page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage and memory-dense cloud server configuration built on the x86_64 architecture using Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor, this instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled. The system includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core, alongside a bundled 2880 GB local NVMe SSD storage volume. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included in this instance profile. Instruction set capabilities include AVX, AVX-512, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, FMA, and SVM virtualization support.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core processing performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2071.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 3078.28. Multi-core performance aligns with expected scaling for a 4-vCPU system, achieving an average Geekbench multi-core score of 4736.0 and an average stress-ng multi-core score of 6154.66. Operational tests demonstrate average Redis SET throughput of 6.17 million operations per second and steady LLM prompt processing for small 135M models at 462.72 tokens per second. Performance trade-offs appear in memory bandwidth metrics, where small-block cached read speeds measure 303.46 GB/sec and uncached read speeds measure 36.73 GB/sec, alongside weak static web serving throughput of 6.28 GB/sec.

The L4aos_v4 architecture provides strong hardware cost efficiency by pairing substantial local NVMe storage capacity directly with a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. This eliminates the need for attached network storage blocks when managing localized data pipelines. Primary workload fits include local database servers, caching nodes, intermediate data staging environments, and single-thread intensive applications requiring quick access to high-capacity local disk space.
description: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a storage and memory-dense cloud server built on x86_64 architecture and Hyper-V virtualization. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz, paired with 32 GB of RAM and 2880 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware benchmarks show strong single-core CPU compute and text processing, complemented by average multi-core performance and average Redis operation throughput. Tested memory bandwidth on uncached reads and static web serving throughput register on the lower end. With an 8 GB RAM per vCPU allocation and extensive local SSD capacity bundled into the hardware profile, the instance provides clear resource density efficiency for localized database engines, memory-bound caching systems, and processing workloads requiring significant local storage performance without relying on network-attached storage volumes.
